lens: Reach and kinematics: what the 5-DoF left arm can actually reach on the table (from g1_body23.urdf link lengths, joint limits and the torso meshes), versus what hackathon/brain/brain.py allows (forearm forced to +x, lane y 0.06-0.30 / x 0.31-0.50), with the torso-collision geometry, the far-reach limit and the open-loop slide error read back from the Oct 19/21 logs. All numbers computed with a stdlib URDF/STL parser and a 4-joint numerical IK in the scratchpad (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-junda-robot-harness/44b035f1-dc0d-4025-a748-1eab1915cdb8/scratchpad/{reach.py,analysis.py,evalmod.py,followup.py,mapcal.py,analysis_out.txt}); nothing run on the robot, no files edited.

findings.claim: The lane is a property of one grasp strategy, not of the arm: forcing the forearm to +x pins the elbow at the can's y + 4.3 cm, so every can with y < 0.10 puts the lower upper arm within 2 cm of the chest's left flank and every can with y < 0.04 puts the elbow INSIDE the chest. That is why the Oct 19 centre-line attempt was blocked and why the lane's inner bound exists.

findings.claim: The far bound (~0.50 m can axis) is physical, not a strategy limit, and the far half of the lane is the worst place to grasp: at can height the elbow can be at most 10.5 cm from the shoulder's vertical, so a level forearm reaches palm distances of only 0.24-0.45 m from (0, 0.10); beyond that the forearm must droop 13-19 deg and the real palm, 0.096 m further along the drooping roll axis, drops 1-2 cm below what the +x constant assumes (and sits 1-1.6 cm higher at the near lane).

DESIGN_REVIEW.md line 20-21 already names the pattern ('pinky 0.9 means the hand is low'; 'thumb 0.9 ... can is forward of the palm').
findings.fix: Correct after every slide step from the measured FK (or the head-camera hand/can offset), targeting the real palm; this also removes most of the need for the calibrated dz.

findings.claim: The tracking-error 'contact' stop fires on events that are not the can, and its fixed 0.015 rad threshold is a shrinking fraction of a baseline that rises with reach, so at the far cans it stops the slide early or on noise.
findings.evidence: live7.log 030059 o1: 'slide: steps 1 contact True (tracking error 0.081 > base 0.065 + 0.015) cmd y 0.168' while the can surface was at y 0.075+0.0275 = 0.1025, i.e. 6.6 cm away, with the hand measured 3.6 cm low and 1.6 cm short after one 1 cm step. Baselines: 0.044-0.050 at model-palm x 0.30-0.32 (024115, both grasped) vs 0.058-0.069 at x 0.36-0.38 (025439, 030059). Computed upper-arm clearance at the 030059 grasp poses is 1.0 and 0.7 cm to the torso box (rubbing plausible); the soft-direction IK re-solved per step (dir_weight 0.5) can also jump elbow branch; q per step is not logged so the two cannot be separated.
findings.fix: Keep contact only as a safety abort at >= 2x the per-pose baseline; stop the slide on the measured palm-to-can offset; log q and tracking error per step so a branch flip is visible.

findings.claim: The IK tolerance of 3.5 cm is larger than the grasp geometry it serves: it accepts solutions that leave the palm up to a full can radius away from the planned point, and it was already the reason the first Oct 19 attempt started from a pose 2.8 cm short.
findings.evidence: brain.py line 26 `--tol 0.035`; line 384 `if res.pos_err > P.tol`. office-grab.md line 7: 'at 44 cm ahead and 7 cm left it was 2.6-2.8 cm short, within the 3.5 cm tolerance used for the attempt'; grab_trials.jsonl trial 1 ik_err 0.0421 refused, later trials 0.0004-0.0061. The palm sits only r+1 cm = 3.75-4.3 cm from the can axis, so a 3.5 cm IK error is 80-95 % of that offset.
findings.fix: With a hard-yaw search the solution either exists or not: set the tolerance to 5 mm on the real palm point and let the search, not the tolerance, absorb reach.

findings.claim: Only one palm family exists on a table for the left hand: palm normal n = d x z-hat (palm to the right of the forearm, thumb up). 'Facing the midline' (psi 0) and 'facing back' (psi 90) are the two ends of that family, not two options; the mirror family (thumb down) needs a 180 deg wrist roll, outside the +/-113 deg limit, and would put the thumb into the table. 'Facing back' is unreachable for table cans because the elbow would have to be 35 cm left of the can.
findings.evidence: URDF left_wrist_roll_joint limits -1.972..+1.972 rad; wrist->palm 0.246 + elbow->wrist 0.101 = 0.346 m forearm-plus-hand; elbow ring radius at can height 0.105 m around (0, 0.10), so psi >= 50 deg fails the IK for every can beyond x ~0.25 (centre-line table: psi 50 err 3.7 mm rising to 44 mm at 90; can (0.30, 0): psi 60 err 6.4 mm). Table surface is only ~6 cm below the can axis (logs: can z 0.14, heights 0.119-0.139, floor 0.98 m); trial 8 with the palm 2 cm below mid-height was the deepest wrap (office-grab.md line 28), so the pinky side already runs ~1 cm above the table.
findings.fix: Make psi the single search variable; derive n and the wrist roll (wrist_roll_for_palm(n)) from it; do not search palm orientations.

findings.claim: The wrist roll is not a limiting joint for the new solutions, but two obstacles are unmodelled: the right arm (for cross-body cans) and the stand's frame (where the elbow now sits).
findings.evidence: Over all accepted cells the required wrist roll differs from the lane-centre pose by -37..+70 deg (centre and right cells -5..-30 deg) against +/-113 deg limits; palm_inward_wrist_roll.left is the calibrated reference (grab_lateral.py `ROLL = arg("--roll", float(cfg.robot.palm_inward_wrist_roll.left))`). The brain parks only the left arm (brain.py lines 515-516 `move_to("left", ...)`) and never reads the right arm's pose; cross-body solutions cross the centre line at x 0.30-0.39. Accepted elbow positions lie at y 0.18-0.30, x 0.00-0.11, z 0.11-0.19 (Map D), beside the hips/ribs where the stand holds the robot; office-grab.md line 45 already blames 'the stand's straps' for stepping artefacts.
findings.fix: Add the right arm as a capsule from its measured joints (r 5 cm) to the clearance test and verify the elbow-to-stand gap in the air test before any cross-body can.

design:
Replace the lane with an elbow-swivel feasibility search, and make the arm model honest.

Inputs per order: the can axis C (x, y, z_mid) and radius r from the head camera; the table plane z_t and edge x_e from the depth image (g1-fetch has fit_plane_ransac); the measured joints of both arms. Model: the g1_body23.urdf left chain (upper arm 0.193 m, elbow-wrist 0.101 m) with the REAL palm point 0.246 m along the wrist roll axis (ee_offset_x 0.15 + the 0.096 calibrated on Oct 19/21). The constant --dx goes away; the IK then places the real palm, and the offset rotates with the forearm instead of being a +x constant that is 1-2 cm wrong at the lane's ends.

Search space: one variable, the forearm yaw psi (+ = toward the midline), psi in {-30 ... +60 deg} in 5 deg steps, visited outward from psi_pref = clamp(10 + (0.09 - y)*100, 0, 50) deg. For each psi: forearm direction d = (cos psi, -sin psi, 0); palm normal n = d x z-hat = (-sin psi, -cos psi, 0), the only thumb-up family (its mirror needs a 180 deg roll and puts the thumb in the table); grasp palm P = C - (r + 0.01) n; pre-grasp P_pre = P - 0.05 n; high waypoints P_pre + 0.12 z-hat. Solve the 4-joint IK (shoulder pitch/roll/yaw, elbow) for P with the roll-axis yaw constrained HARD to psi (not dir_weight 0.5), seeded from the previous psi's solution; wrist roll from wrist_roll_for_palm(n). The forearm pitch is an outcome, one value per psi; read it, do not search it.

Torso and obstacle model (pelvis frame): the torso as 2 cm z-band boxes computed once from the URDF meshes (at z 0.10-0.16: x -0.06..+0.07, y +/-0.098; chest +/-0.108 at z 0.26); links as capsules: lower 40 % of the upper arm r 0.04, forearm r 0.04, wrist-to-palm (BrainCo hand) r 0.05; the right arm as a capsule from its measured joints r 0.05; the table as z < z_t for x > x_e; the hand bottom as palm z - 0.045. Clearance = minimum capsule-to-box distance over 12 samples per segment. Hard safety kept: nothing within 0.30 m straight ahead at chest height, and a tracking-error rise above 2x the per-pose baseline aborts the motion (an abort, not a 'contact').

Acceptance, applied to the grasp pose, the pre-grasp, the five 1 cm slide poses between them and both high waypoints: IK error <= 5 mm (not 35 mm); |forearm pitch| <= 15 deg; lower-upper-arm clearance >= 3 cm (log-calibrated: 1.7-3.4 cm grasped, 0.7-1.0 rubbed, -4.3 blocked), forearm >= 4 cm, hand >= 6 cm; right-arm capsule >= 5 cm; forearm underside >= 2 cm above the table beyond x_e; hand bottom >= 1 cm above the table; every joint >= 10 deg from its limit; required wrist roll within limits. Choose the accepted psi with the smallest |pitch| (ties: smaller |psi|). Refuse only when no psi passes, and say which constraint failed ('too far for my arm', 'my elbow would hit my chest'). On the computed map this turns 54 usable cells into 202 (3 cm grid, z 0.13): the whole lane, the centre line to x 0.48, and 12 cm right of centre at x <= 0.36.

What each solution implies for the approach (the hand's C always faces the can along n): psi ~0 (lane cells, y 0.12-0.24) is today's lateral slide from the left. psi 20-35 (centre line, y -0.03..+0.09) comes from the can's left-front, moving right-and-back at that angle, fingers pointing forward-right, elbow 18-23 cm left of centre beside the ribs, shoulder abducted 13-31 deg and yawed 23-37 deg inward, elbow joint near its 90 deg zero. psi 40-70 (5-18 cm right of centre, x <= 0.36) is a diagonal sweep toward the body with the hand passing >= 6 cm in front of the chest. psi < 0 (y > 0.24) comes from the can's left-rear moving right-forward. The pre-grasp is always 5 cm back along n, so the slide never crosses the torso box.

Motion: raise, high above P_pre, lower to P_pre, then slide along n in 1 cm steps with a measured-FK correction after every step (the open-loop slide sags 2.1-3.6 cm in z and 0.6-1.8 cm in x, more at long reach), all IK solves seeded from the previous q with psi interpolated from the park pose's yaw to the target so the elbow never flips branch; log q, measured FK and tracking error per step.

Where the collision risk actually is: (1) the lower upper arm against the chest's left flank (y 0.097-0.108 at z 0.12-0.26) whenever the shoulder roll is below about +5 deg, which the +x forearm forces for every can with y < 0.10; (2) the elbow inside the chest's front-left corner (x < 0.07, y < 0.14) for cans with y < 0.04 under the same strategy. With psi >= 20 the shoulder abducts and the elbow moves to y 0.18-0.30; the remaining risks are the stand frame at the new elbow positions and the right arm for cross-body cans, both checked in the air.

Safe validation in the stand, in order: (1) offline replay of the 14 logged can positions through the new test (13 accepted at psi 5-35; the Oct 19 one rejected at psi 0 and accepted at 35) and FK agreement between this chain and g1-fetch ArmKinematics at five poses to the millimetre; (2) --dry prints psi, q, elbow position and all clearances for the detected can; (3) air test without can or table: three targets (0.38/0.15, 0.35/0.00, 0.30/-0.05), half speed, hand open, spotter on L2+B, owner measures the elbow-to-torso and elbow-to-stand gaps by hand at the pre-grasp (expect >= 5 cm at psi 30) and the head camera must show the hand box at P_pre; (4) cans at the lane, then the centre line, then right of centre. Thresholds are then set from measured gaps, not guesses, and never again from distances on one table.
first_experiments: Offline, no robot: port the swivel search to g1-fetch's ArmKinematics (same URDF chain), check its FK against this scratch model at 5 poses (expect mm agreement for the 0.15 palm point), then replay the 14 logged can positions; expected: all 12 grasped/missed positions accepted at psi 5-35 deg with >= 4.8 cm upper-arm clearance, the Oct 19 [0.347, 0.008] rejected at psi 0 (-4.3 cm) and accepted at 35 deg, the 030059 poses flagged at 0.7-1.0 cm for psi 0. This calibrates the clearance thresholds before anything moves.

Air test in the stand (no can, no table, hand open, half speed, spotter on L2+B): for three targets (0.38/0.15, 0.35/0.00, 0.30/-0.05 at z 0.13) run high waypoint -> pre-grasp -> 5 cm slide along n with the search-chosen psi (expect ~0, ~30, ~45 deg); log q, measured FK and tracking error per step; owner measures the elbow-torso and elbow-stand gaps by hand at each pre-grasp (model predicts 6.3 cm upper-arm clearance at the centre line, psi 30) and confirms the head camera sees the hand (Gemma 'robot's white hand' box) at the pre-grasp. Pass: tracking-error baseline <= 0.05 rad at all three, no rub.

Sag map: at four reaches (model palm x 0.30, 0.36, 0.42, 0.46 at y 0.15-0.20, z 0.14) command a cart_move without correction, hold 2 s, record measured-minus-commanded in x and z (logs predict -2.1 to -3.6 cm z, -0.6 to -1.8 cm x), then repeat with a per-step measured-FK correction during a 5 cm slide; pass when the slide-end error is under 1 cm at all four. Decides whether the slide needs the camera loop or proprioception suffices.

Real-palm model check: set ee_offset_x to 0.246, remove --dx, and repeat the Oct 21 jog at two reaches (can 0.35 and 0.47 ahead): the step at which the owner sees the can centred on the palm should now be step 0 at both, instead of -0.097 at 0.478 and a different value nearer; a residual > 1 cm between the two reaches means the palm point is off the roll axis and needs a z/y component.

First centre-line grasp: one can at (0.35, 0.00) and one at today's refused position (0.40, 0.03), psi from the search (expect 25-35 and 20-25), with the per-step correction on; success criterion is the lane grasps' stall signature (thumb 0.1-0.2, fingers 0.4-0.55) on 3 of 4 tries, elbow-torso gap >= 5 cm throughout.

lens: Grasp strategy and visual servoing: why the Oct 19-21 grasps missed or held, derived from grab_trials.jsonl, live1-7.log, order_*.jsonl and the C922/head frames; and the closed-loop hand-to-can strategy for the 5-DoF left arm (no wrist pitch) with the BrainCo hand, measured in the D435i head camera.

findings.claim: The hand is placed open-loop in the arm model's frame: the model's palm point is ~10 cm short of the real palm, the error changes with configuration, and the 'measured' position used for the two proprioceptive corrections is forward kinematics of the same wrong model, so the corrections only make the model agree with itself. The one-frame hand-and-can measurement that existed on Oct 19 was dropped.
findings.evidence: brain.py:257-258 `hand_meas` = kin.fk(measured q); :260-274 `move()` drives goal minus that FK; :21 `--dx -0.096` is the whole calibration. jog_today.log: commanded 2 cm steps gave palm offsets -0.118, -0.097, -0.082, -0.069, -0.068, -0.066, i.e. the hand stopped advancing at x 0.41 for a can at 0.478 (reach limit inside the 'measured' loop). xr_teleoperate/teleop/robot_control/robot_arm_ik.py:358-364 puts the 23-DoF end effector 0.20 m from left_wrist_roll_joint; g1-fetch uses 0.15 (task brief), the jog implies ~0.25 to the palm centre. grab_lateral.py:75-103 measured the Gemma box of 'the robot's white hand' (box_to_point, shrink 0.5) and the YOLOE can in the same head frame and corrected x,z; office-mon/attempt2_pregrasp_boxes.jpg shows both boxes in one frame. grab_loop.py and brain.py contain no such step (DESIGN_REVIEW.md:7-11).
findings.fix: Close the loop in the head camera: measure the hand feature and the can axis in one aligned RGB-D frame, servo the difference (design section). Keep the proprioceptive correction only as the inner loop that holds a visually set setpoint against joint tracking error.

findings.claim: The slide throws away the pre-grasp correction: the first slide step re-commands the nominal pre-grasp trajectory, so the palm drops 2.1-3.6 cm in z (and 0.5-1.8 cm back in x) on every attempt, more at far reach. Monday's successes hid this with dz +0.03; Tuesday's default dz 0 exposed it, which is why the pinky (lowest finger) read 0.9 in the near-misses.
findings.evidence: brain.py:264-270 `cmd = cmd + err` then set_target(q of cmd); :402 `cur = pre.copy()`; :406 `solve_pose(..., cur, ...)` uses the nominal pre, never cmd. Same in grab_loop.py:186-191. Logs, pre measured z -> slide measured z: live1 0.140->0.116 and 0.138->0.116; live2 0.133->0.110; live3 0.137->0.116, 0.140->0.117; live4 0.144->0.121, 0.139->0.118 (x 0.29-0.32: -2.1 to -2.4 cm); live6 0.133->0.101, 0.139->0.108; live7 0.136->0.100, 0.136->0.102 (x 0.36-0.38: -3.1 to -3.6 cm, x -1.5 to -1.8 cm). The uncorrected 'high' waypoint errors match: 0.031-0.035 near, 0.043-0.046 far. Monday grab_trials.jsonl pre_measured vs slide_measured: -1.2 to -3.7 cm; trials 5-7 ran dz +0.03 (brain.py:22 defaults dz to 0.0).
findings.fix: Start the slide from the corrected command (carry `cmd` out of move() into the slide) and re-apply the measured joint-tracking correction in z and x at every step; in v2 the visual loop sets the setpoint and this inner loop holds it.

findings.claim: The misses have two stall signatures that map to geometry, not to luck: (a) thumb 0.9 with index/middle/ring stalled ~0.5 and pinky 0.9 = the fingers reach the can but the thumb sweeps behind it and the pinky under it, i.e. the can is forward of the palm centre and the palm is low; (b) all fingers 0.9 with thumb 0.59 = the hand closed on nothing (passed beside, or pushed the can).

design:
Frames and pose. Pelvis frame: x ahead, y left, z up. Per attempt a grasp frame (f, n, z): f = forearm direction (cos t, -sin t, 0), n = palm normal pointing at the can (-sin t, -cos t, 0), t chosen by IK feasibility from 0 deg (today) up to 45 deg inward so the forearm crosses in front of the torso instead of running beside it. The hand is open with the thumb opposed (THUMB_PRE) from the pre-grasp onward, so every hand feature is a fixed point in the hand frame.

Closure pose (from the 12 holds and the jog): the can axis at the palm centre, between the thumb base and the finger knuckles; the palm face R+1 cm from the axis along -n; the palm centre 1.5 cm below the can's mid-height, never lower than mid-height minus 2 cm (the pinky must stay above the can's bottom). The fingers wrap the far side, the thumb closes from behind. The approach is a straight line along +n at that height; the pre-grasp is the closure pose minus 3 cm along n (not 5: keeps the hand in the image).

Measurement pipeline (one aligned RGB-D head frame, flush 3). Can: YOLOE 'soda can' box and mask (105-135 ms); median depth of the central 50 percent, deprojected into the pelvis frame = front surface; axis = +R along the viewing ray's horizontal projection; R from the box width (55/66 mm) as now. Table: RANSAC plane on the depth band around the can's base; grasp z = z_table + h/2 - 0.015. Hand: all depth points higher than z_table + 2 cm inside a window of +/-15 cm around the FK-predicted palm (the FK bias of about +10 cm in x is inside the window), minus the can mask dilated 10 px; the largest cluster is the hand. Three features, each a fixed hand-frame point while the hand is open and the thumb opposed: the fingertip extent (max along f), the thumb tip (min along n... the point nearest the can), and the median z. Setpoint K = the offset of these features from the can axis at the owner-approved 'centred on the palm' pose (one jog, stored as a hand constant; this is a hardware calibration, not a scene distance). Error e = (can_axis + K) - hand_features, in f, n and z. Cross-check once per grasp with the Gemma box of 'the robot's hand with the red strap' (0.85 s; box_to_point shrink 0.5); if the two disagree by > 3 cm, abort the servo. Expected accuracy: D435 relative depth at 0.5 m 3-5 mm, YOLOE can point repeats within 7 mm, hand cluster extents about 1 cm; relative offset error about 1 cm, inside the +/-2 cm palm window seen in the trials. If the cluster scatters more than that, a 5 cm ArUco tag on the back of the glove (cv2.aruco, ~30 px at this range) replaces the cluster features.

Servo loop. Measure e; command cmd += clip(e_f, e_z, +/-3 cm) through the IK with x_dir = f, palm = n; settle 0.6 s; the inner proprioceptive loop holds the joint tracking error (this is what finding 2 lost); re-measure. Converged when |e_f| and |e_z| < 1 cm on two consecutive frames. Budget 3 iterations (about 1.2 s each: frame, YOLOE, cluster, move) = the 4 s pause it replaces. Not converged, hand not found, or hand within 40 px of the image edge: retreat up and say so.

Approach (replaces the blind slide). Two half-steps along +n sized from the measured gap e_n; re-measure between them; abort if the can axis moved > 1.5 cm (pushed) or the hand left the window. Close when the measured gap < 1 cm. Contact (tracking error +0.015 over its base) and lag > 1.2 cm stay as stop conditions only; no commanded press beyond gap 0.

Closure and stall corrections. Stages as today (thumb opposed, fingers 0.9, thumb 0.9), hand state logged after each stage. Verdict: thumb < 0.3 and at least 3 fingers in (0.25, 0.70). On failure, one targeted correction from the pattern: thumb 0.9 with fingers stalled = can forward of the palm -> open, +3 cm along f, re-close; pinky 0.9 alone -> open, +2 cm z; all 0.9 -> YOLOE re-detect: moved > 2 cm = pushed -> re-locate, else -3 cm along f. One correction, then the assisted path.

Lift verification. Lift 6 cm with the inner loop; one head frame; the can box's 3D point must rise by lift +/- 2 cm and move with the hand cluster. If not, it is a miss whatever the stall says. Gemma's third-person yes/no becomes a displayed opinion, not a gate.

Handover. Offer pose computed to lie inside the head camera's view (from the camera pose in the URDF: 47.6 deg down, half-FOV 27.4 x 21.3 deg), about 25 cm ahead, 17 cm left, 24 cm up in model coordinates, which already satisfies it. Release on any of: a new depth cluster within 6 cm of the can in two consecutive frames (the guest's hand) confirmed by one Gemma yes/no on the head frame; a tug (any stalled finger moving > 0.03 from its held value while the fresh setpoint is re-sent each cycle); a let-go transcript, never recorded within 4 s of TTS. Then thumb back, fingers open.

Hard safeties that stay. Nothing within 0.30 m straight ahead at chest height moves the arm forward; IK error > 3.5 cm or tracking-error base > 0.06 rad means re-plan with another forearm direction or refuse; max 3 cm per servo correction and 3 iterations; contact and lag stops; up-first retreat over the measured table edge; park pose; operator keys and the safe shutdown. Every iteration logs frame path, can point, hand features, e, command and FK, so the next miss is diagnosed from the log rather than by changing a delta.
first_experiments: Kill test for the servo (no can motion, decides everything else): hand at the pre-grasp 3 cm beside the can at three can positions (x 0.30, 0.38, 0.46; y 0.10-0.18), 5 head frames each; log the hand cluster features, the Gemma hand box point and the YOLOE can axis, the measured palm-to-can offset and the model's FK offset. Pass: frame-to-frame scatter of the offset under 1 cm and the measured-minus-model offset about +0.10 m in x, changing by 2-4 cm across positions as DESIGN_REVIEW predicts. Then command one correction from the measurement and re-measure: residual under 1 cm in two iterations. Fail (scatter > 1.5 cm or hand not found): switch to the ArUco tag on the glove before building anything else.

One-line slide fix plus per-stage hand logging: carry the corrected command into the slide (or re-apply the z/x tracking correction each step), log the six finger q after each closure stage, and re-run three grasps with yesterday's dx -0.096 and dz 0. Pass: measured z stays within 1 cm of the pre-grasp during the slide (today -2.1 to -3.6 cm), and the finger q before and after the thumb lock answer the owner's loosening question.

The full servo-and-approach loop on one can at three positions including one 7-8 cm from the centre line with the forearm rotated 30 deg inward: log per-iteration offsets, the gap at closure, the stall state and the result. Target: 9 of 9 holds with no parameter changes between positions; any miss must be explained by the per-iteration log.

Lift and handover in the head camera: on 5 holds and 2 deliberate misses (hand 4 cm forward), record the can point before and after the lift (expect +6 cm only on holds); then 5 handovers at the computed offer pose with a guest reaching in, scoring the depth-cluster cue, the Gemma yes/no on the head frame and the tug cue separately, with the time to release and any false release.

Stall-pattern corrections: induce each miss class on purpose (hand 3 cm forward, 2 cm low, can pushed) five times each and apply the single mapped correction; pass if the correction recovers 4 of 5 in each class, which also validates the pattern-to-geometry mapping on a day other than the one it was derived from.

lens: Fragility and process: where every number in hackathon/brain/brain.py and spikes/scripts/grab_loop.py came from, why a stack "verified" on Monday missed for an hour on Tuesday, and what rules and harness stop it recurring.

The brain computes the measured palm position at every slide step and discards its z: the palm ends 2.4-4.0 cm below the can's mid-height in every Tuesday pick.

Rules.

1. One calibration source. hackathon/brain/calib.json is the only place a geometric number lives. Each entry: value, unit, method (script name), date, conditions (table height, can type, pose x/y/z, n), log path. brain.py loads it, prints the table at start, and refuses to run when an entry is missing, older than the table setup, or measured at a different table height than the one preflight finds. Runtime measurements (table plane, can size, palm-to-can offset, slide z, contact baseline) are never stored there; they are logged per order.

2. Parameters are named, not numeric. A Params dataclass with a class tag (measured, calibrated, policy) replaces CLI defaults; a literal in a motion line fails review. The view shows the active table.

3. Loop-eval protocol for any change: reproduce the failure from the logs (replay evaluator over order_NN.jsonl and frames); instrument (per-step hand_meas x/y/z, tracking error, hand state, head frame at pre, mid-slide, closed, lifted); isolate one variable; N >= 5 per configuration across >= 3 can positions; report a per-stage table (located, feasible, pre-grasp error, slide-end palm-to-can x/z, contact reason, hand-state pattern, lift, release) with n. 'Verified' means this table exists with identical parameters; a streak across configurations is reported per configuration.

4. On the robot: hypotheses are written before the run; no parameter change without a logged hypothesis and a prediction; at most one change between runs; after three misses stop and read the logs, no fourth attempt. Battery and owner time are the budget: a robot block is an experiment list, never design.

5. Session boundaries. One session per phase: brief writing, offline build and replay validation, robot block, post-mortem. Each starts from the written brief and ends by updating it. Start a fresh session whenever the plan is about to change on the robot or the session has consumed a robot block. The brief must contain: hardware facts (joints, hand, camera pose), the calibration table with dates, the failure-signature table (hand-state pattern to cause), the per-stage results so far with n, the experiment cards for the block, the stop rules, and what counts as done.

6. Before any robot time the owner sees: the experiment card (hypothesis, the one variable, N, success criterion, abort rule); the replay result on logged data; the calibration table with dates; the geometric preflight output (table plane, can measured, IK feasible with clearance, hand visible to the head camera at the pre-grasp); the reachable map for the current stand position.

Harness. brain/eval/replay.py recomputes localisation, feasibility and the verify rule from stored orders and reports what the new code would have done; brain/eval/stages.py prints the per-stage table from runs/; brain/eval/handstates.jsonl holds labelled states for fitting the verify rule; brain/calibrate/ holds the jog, the table-plane fit, the hand-in-camera measurement and the torso box measurement, each writing calib.json with provenance. The view shows the measured palm-to-can offset live so the owner can see the loop closing.
first_experiments: Hand-in-head-camera localisation at the pre-grasp, no slide, no can motion: at six can positions (x 0.35 and 0.45; y 0.08, 0.15, 0.22) move to the pre-grasp, take one D435i frame, measure the palm (depth blob or Gemma box of the white hand) and the can axis in the pelvis frame, log measured-vs-FK offset in x and z per position. Decides whether the servo loop is viable; expect 3-4 cm disagreement that changes with pose.

Sag and contact-baseline map with no can on the table: at the same six positions run pre-grasp then the full 1 cm slide, logging hand_meas x/y/z and tracking error per step. Gives the z drop and the baseline as functions of pose and tests whether the 0.015 rad rule false-fires with nothing to touch (it did at 030059 step 1).

Verify-rule fit: 20 owner placements of a can in the open hand at varied depth and height, 5 empty closes, 5 closes with the can at the fingertips; record the full hand state after each stage, label, and fit the rule; during a 10 s hold log closure with and without the thumb lock to answer the owner's thumb question.

Free-forearm feasibility: offline, run the g1-fetch IK over the can grid with forearm yaw 0-45 deg inward and palm toward the midline or the body, with a torso box measured from the URDF and one tape measurement; print the reachable map; then one on-robot check without a can at y 0.03 and 0.07 with the elbow rotated in, owner watching for torso contact.

Description-based ordering on the Mac: the two-can head frames plus 12 recorded clips (fruit picture, flavour, brand, 'the tall one', in three languages) through the numbered-list prompt; report accuracy with n and latency, before any robot time.
